title: Maps of finitely presented algebras over a directed colimit of rings come from a stage
statement: Let $(\Lambda,\le)$ be a directed set and $(R_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ a directed system of commutative rings (ring maps $R_\lambda\to R_\mu$ for $\lambda\le\mu$, the identity for $\lambda=\mu$, compatible with composition) with colimit $R=\varinjlim_\lambda R_\lambda$ in the category of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $\lambda\in\Lambda$ and let $A$, $A'$ be finitely presented $R_\lambda$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. For $\mu\ge\lambda$ put $A_\mu=A\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu$, $A'_\mu=A'\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu$ ($R_\mu$-algebras), and $A_R=A\otimes_{R_\lambda}R$, $A'_R=A'\otimes_{R_\lambda}R$; identify $A_\mu\otimes_{R_\mu}R=A_R$ and $A'_\mu\otimes_{R_\mu}R=A'_R$ by $(a\otimes r)\otimes r'\mapsto a\otimes\bar r r'$. (2) For every homomorphism of $R$-algebras $u:A_R\to A'_R$ there are $\mu\ge\lambda$ and a homomorphism of $R_\mu$-algebras $u_\mu:A_\mu\to A'_\mu$ with $u_\mu\otimes1_R=u$. (3) If $v,w:A\to A'$ are homomorphisms of $R_\lambda$-algebras with $v\otimes1_R=w\otimes1_R$, then $v\otimes1_{R_\mu}=w\otimes1_{R_\mu}$ for some $\mu\ge\lambda$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 05N9 (lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras, algebra.tex line 32178), parts (2) and (3); its proof refers to Lemma Tag 05N8 (lemma-algebra-map-property-in-colimit)

proof.text: *Step 1 (the base-changed target is a colimit).* Restrict the system to the directed upper set $\Lambda_{\ge\lambda}=\{\mu:\mu\ge\lambda\}$, which is cofinal: for any $\nu$ choose a common upper bound of $\nu$ and $\lambda$. Write $B_\mu=A'\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu$ and $B=A'\otimes_{R_\lambda}R$. We verify that $B$, with the maps $B_\mu\to B$, is a colimit in commutative $R_\lambda$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For any commutative $R_\lambda$-algebra $T$, an $R_\lambda$-algebra map $B_\mu\to T$ is, by the tensor-product pushout property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], exactly a pair of $R_\lambda$-algebra maps $A'\to T$ and $R_\mu\to T$. A compatible family over $\mu\ge\lambda$ has one common map $A'\to T$ and a compatible family $R_\mu\to T$; the colimit property of $R$ yields exactly one $R_\lambda$-algebra map $R\to T$ for the latter. Such pairs correspond by the same pushout property to maps $B\to T$, and the correspondence respects the coprojections. Thus $B=\varinjlim_{\mu\ge\lambda}B_\mu$ in $R_\lambda$-algebras and, by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise](1), also in commutative rings. The upper-set colimit of the $R_\mu$ is $R$: a cocone on the upper set extends to the whole directed system by choosing a common upper bound with $\lambda$, and independence of that choice follows at a further common upper bound. (This is the base-change colimit used in the proof of Stacks 05N8(3).)

source.place: Lemma Tag 05N8 (lemma-algebra-map-property-in-colimit, lines 32149-32166), proof of (3), using the colimit of base changes; Lemma Tag 05N9 (lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras), proof line 32215

proof.text: *Step 2 (a map descends: clause (2)).* Choose a presentation $A\cong R_\lambda[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ from [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Restrict $u:A_R\to A'_R=B$ to $A\to A_R$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$; this is an $R_\lambda$-algebra map $g:A\to B$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit] to $R_\lambda$, the presentation of $A$, and the colimit $(B_\mu)_{\mu\ge\lambda}$ from step 1. It gives $\mu\ge\lambda$ and an $R_\lambda$-algebra map $g_\mu:A\to B_\mu$ whose composite to $B$ is $g$. Since $B_\mu$ is an $R_\mu$-algebra, the base-change adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-base-change-universal-property] extends $g_\mu$ uniquely to an $R_\mu$-algebra map $u_\mu:A\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\to B_\mu$ with $u_\mu(a\otimes r)=g_\mu(a)(1\otimes r)$. Its extension to $R$ agrees with $u$ on $a\otimes1$ by construction and on $1\otimes r$ since both are $R$-algebra maps. Pure tensors are products of these elements, so $u_\mu\otimes1_R=u$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05N9 (lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras, lines 32187-32193), proof line 32215 via Lemma Tag 05N8 (lemma-algebra-map-property-in-colimit), part (3), lines 32119-32123 and 32149-32166

proof.text: *Step 3 (equality descends: clause (3)).* Choose generators $x_1,\dots,x_n$ of $A$ as an $R_\lambda$-algebra from its finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and put $d_j=v(x_j)-w(x_j)\in A'$. The hypothesis $v\otimes1_R=w\otimes1_R$ gives $1\otimes d_j=0$ in $A'\otimes_{R_\lambda}R$ for each $j$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise](2) with initial index $\lambda$ and $M_0=A'$ as an $R_\lambda$-module: for each $j$ there is $\mu_j\ge\lambda$ where $1\otimes d_j=0$ in $A'\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_{\mu_j}$. Directedness gives a common $\mu\ge\mu_1,\dots,\mu_n$; the same equalities hold there by the transition maps. The maps $v\otimes1_{R_\mu}$ and $w\otimes1_{R_\mu}$ agree on $x_j\otimes1$, and both are $R_\mu$-algebra maps, hence agree on $1\otimes r$ for $r\in R_\mu$. These elements generate $A\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu$ as a ring, so the two maps agree. For $n=0$ they agree on the coefficient ring already, and one may take $\mu=\lambda$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_map_of_finitePresentation_colimit {Λ : Type u} [Preorder Λ] [IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)] (F : Λ ⥤ CommRingCat.{v}) [HasColimit F] (i : Λ) (A : Type w) (A' : Type z) [CommRing A] [CommRing A'] [Algebra (F.obj i) A] [Algebra (F.obj i) A'] [Algebra.FinitePresentation (F.obj i) A] [Algebra.FinitePresentation (F.obj i) A'] : let S := F.obj i let R := colimit F letI : Algebra S R := (colimit.ι F i).hom.toAlgebra letI : Algebra R (A ⊗[S] R) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra letI : Algebra R (A' ⊗[S] R) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (∀ u : (A ⊗[S] R) →ₐ[R] (A' ⊗[S] R), ∃ (μ : Λ) (h : i ≤ μ), letI : Algebra S (F.obj μ) := (F.map (homOfLE h)).hom.toAlgebra let t : F.obj μ →ₐ[S] R := { (colimit.ι F μ).hom with commutes' := fun s ↦ congrArg (fun f : F.obj i ⟶ colimit F ↦ f s) (colimit.w F (homOfLE h)) } letI : Algebra (F.obj μ) (A ⊗[S] (F.obj μ)) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra letI : Algebra (F.obj μ) (A' ⊗[S] (F.obj μ)) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra ∃ uμ : (A ⊗[S] (F.obj μ)) →ₐ[F.obj μ] (A' ⊗[S] (F.obj μ)), ∀ x : A ⊗[S] (F.obj μ), Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S A') t (uμ x) = u (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S A) t x)) ∧ (∀ v w : A →ₐ[S] A', Algebra.TensorProduct.map v (AlgHom.id S R) = Algebra.TensorProduct.map w (AlgHom.id S R) → ∃ (μ : Λ) (h : i ≤ μ), letI : Algebra S (F.obj μ) := (F.map (homOfLE h)).hom.toAlgebra Algebra.TensorProduct.map v (AlgHom.id S (F.obj μ)) = Algebra.TensorProduct.map w (AlgHom.id S (F.obj μ)))
